newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan says in talks on $350 mln Turkey credit.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan says in talks on $350 mln Turkey credit.

text.p: Turkey is in talks with Kazakhstan to provide a $350 million credit, Kazakh Deputy Foreign Minister Nurlan Danenov said on Monday.
Danenov, who spoke at the start of a two-day visit by Turkish President Suleyman Demirel to the former Soviet republic, did not give any further details on the credit.
"Kazakhstan has already used its first credit of $200 million, granted earlier by Turkey, and now there are talks on a further credit," Danenov told journalists in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
He said Turkish investment in Kazakhstan since independence in 1991 totalled about $1.2 billion.
Turkish companies are active in trade and construction, though they have a lower profile than American oil majors investing in the vast, oil-rich republic of 16.9 million people.

Demirel opened a new Turkish-built hotel with 600 rooms in Almaty on Monday. Turkish firms are also carrying out construction work in Kazakhstan's future capital, Akmola, about 1,200 km (745 miles) northwest of Almaty.
